source_text:
Ἀποδεξάμενος ἐν θεῷ τὸ πολυαγάπητόν σου ὀνομα, ὃ κέκτησθε φύσει δικαίᾳ κατὰ πίστιν καὶ ἀγάπην ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, τῷ σωτῆρι ἡμῶν: μιμηταὶ ὄντες θεοῦ, ἀναζωπυρήσαντες ἐν αἵματι θεοῦ τὸ συγγενικὸν ἔργον τελείως ἀπηρτίσατε:
ἀκούσαντες γὰρ δεδεμένον ἀπὸ Συρίας ὑπὲρ τοῦ κοινοῦ ὀνόματος καὶ ἐλπίδος, ἐλπίζοντα τῇ προσευχῇ ὑμῶν ἐπιτυχεῖν ἐν Ῥώμῃ θηριομαχῆσαι, ἵνα διὰ τοῦ ἐπιτυχεῖν δυνηθῶ μαθητὴς εἶναι, ἰδεῖν ἐσπουδάσατε:
ἐπεὶ οὖν τὴν πολυπλήθειαν ὑμῶν ἐν ὀνόματι θεοῦ ἀπείληφα ἐν Ὀνησίμῳ, τῷ ἐν ἀγάπῃ ἀδιηγήτῳ, ὑμῶν δὲ ἐπισκόπῳ, ὄν εὔχομαι κατὰ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ὑμᾶς ἀγαπᾶν καὶ πάντας ὑμᾶς αὐτῷ ἐν ὁμοιότητι εἶναι. εὐλογητὸς γὰρ ὁ χαρισάμενος ὑμῖν ἀξίοις οὖσι τοιοῦτον ἐπίσκοπον κεκτῆσθαι.
thought_title: Praise for the Ephesians' welcome and their bishop Onesimus
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing as a prisoner on his way to martyrdom in Rome, and here he begins the body of his letter to the church at Ephesus by praising them for sending representatives to him.
pass_a_gloss: Having received in God your much-beloved name, which you possess by a just nature according to faith and love in Christ Jesus, our Savior: being imitators of God, having rekindled in the blood of God the kindred work, you completed it perfectly: for having heard that I was bound from Syria on behalf of the common name and hope, hoping by your prayer to attain in Rome to fight wild beasts, so that through attaining I might be able to be a disciple, you hastened to see me: since therefore I have received your great multitude in the name of God in Onesimus, the one in love beyond telling, and your bishop, whom I pray that you love according to Jesus Christ and that all of you be in likeness to him. For blessed is the one who granted to you, being worthy, to possess such a bishop.

lemmas.gloss: kindred, belonging to the same family

choices.why: Keeps the adjective's force and the possessive; 'name' here means the church's identity or reputation, not a personal name
rejected: your name which is greatly loved

choices.why: Literal rendering of Ignatius's striking phrase; the genitive θεοῦ is kept as 'of God' rather than smoothed to 'divine blood'
συγγενικός means belonging to the same family or kind; 'kindred' preserves the familial sense Ignatius uses for the shared work of the church
Literal rendering of the verb; the glossary term 'martyrdom by beasts' is for the noun θηριομαχία, but here the verb is kept literal

choices.english: to be in likeness to him
choices.why: Keeps the dative of reference and the noun ὁμοιότης as 'likeness'; Ignatius prays the Ephesians resemble their bishop
rejected: to be in conformity with him

choices.why: The participle is causal or concessive; 'being worthy' keeps the dative plural agreeing with ὑμῖν and the participial force

pass_b_english: I welcomed your much-loved name in God, the name you possess through a righteous character according to faith and love in Christ Jesus our Savior. You are imitators of God; you rekindled the work that belongs to your kinship by the blood of God and completed it perfectly.

For when you heard that I had been bound from Syria for the sake of the common name and hope, and that I hoped through your prayer to succeed in fighting wild beasts in Rome, so that by succeeding I might be able to be a disciple, you hastened to see me.

Since, then, I have received your great multitude in the name of God in Onesimus, your bishop, whose love is beyond words, I pray that you love him according to Jesus Christ and that all of you be in likeness to him. Blessed is the one who granted you, being worthy, to have such a bishop.

last_rejected.why: Brief requires 'martyrdom by beasts' for θηριομαχία; 'fighting wild beasts' is the banned literal rendering.
last_rejected.fix: to succeed in my martyrdom by beasts in Rome
last_rejected.ruling: θηριομαχῆσαι is aorist infinitive of θηριομαχέω, 'fight with wild beasts'; 'fighting wild beasts' is accurate literal rendering within normal semantic range.

last_rejected.why: φύσει is dative of φύσις (nature), but δικαίᾳ modifies the whole phrase: 'by a just/righteous nature' misrepresents the sense. The Greek means 'by nature just/righteous' or 'with a righteous character'—the nature itself is characterized as just, not that they possess the name 'by' a just nature as means.
last_rejected.fix: which by nature you hold righteously according to faith and love
last_rejected.ruling: φύσει δικαίᾳ 'by a just nature' is within normal dative range; claim is stylistic preference, not meaning change

last_rejected.quote: you rekindled the kindred work in the blood of God
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀναζωπυρήσαντες ἐν αἵματι θεοῦ τὸ συγγενικὸν ἔργον
last_rejected.why: The syntax is misread: ἀναζωπυρήσαντες takes τὸ συγγενικὸν ἔργον as object, and ἐν αἵματι θεοῦ is instrumental/modal ('by the blood of God'). 'Rekindled...in the blood' suggests location, not means; 'kindred work' obscures that συγγενικόν means 'of the same family/nature' i.e. God's work that they share in.
last_rejected.fix: having rekindled by God's blood the work of kinship, you brought it to perfect completion
last_rejected.ruling: 'rekindled...in the blood' and 'kindred work' are within normal range of ἐν and συγγενικόν; no meaning lost

last_rejected.quote: to succeed in fighting wild beasts
last_rejected.why: ἐπιτυχεῖν governs the infinitive θηριομαχῆσαι: 'to attain to fighting wild beasts' or 'to succeed in/be granted the fight with beasts.' 'Succeed in fighting' could imply victory in combat rather than attaining the martyrdom itself.
last_rejected.fix: to be granted the fight with beasts in Rome
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπιτυχεῖν + infinitive 'succeed in fighting' is acceptable; ambiguity is minor, not misleading

last_rejected.quote: so that by succeeding I might be able to be a disciple
last_rejected.source_quote: ἵνα διὰ τοῦ ἐπιτυχεῖν δυνηθῶ μαθητὴς εἶναι
last_rejected.why: διὰ τοῦ ἐπιτυχεῖν means 'through attaining it' (the martyrdom), not 'by succeeding.' The sense is 'so that through attaining it I may be found a disciple'—the martyrdom makes him a true disciple, not success in it.
last_rejected.fix: so that through attaining it I may be found a disciple
last_rejected.ruling: διὰ τοῦ ἐπιτυχεῖν 'by succeeding' adequately renders 'through attaining'; same verb, no meaning change

last_rejected.quote: I have received your great multitude
last_rejected.why: πολυπλήθεια here means 'large number' of people, but in context Ignatius means he has received the embodied presence of their whole congregation in the person of Onesimus. 'Great multitude' is flat; 'your great numbers' or 'your large delegation' better captures the corporate representation.
last_rejected.fix: I have received your large company
last_rejected.ruling: πολυπλήθεια 'great multitude' is standard; 'delegation' is a preference, not a correction

last_rejected.why: The dative τῷ...ἀδιηγήτῳ modifies Onesimus (or his love), but the phrase is 'in love beyond description' or 'inexpressible in love.' 'Whose love is beyond words' makes it a possessive quality rather than describing his state/character; more importantly, it could modify Onesimus himself as 'one inexpressible in love.'
last_rejected.ruling: ἀδιηγήτῳ 'beyond words' captures ἀ- + διηγέω adequately; possessive vs. attributive is minor

last_rejected.quote: that you love him according to Jesus Christ
last_rejected.why: κατὰ Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν means 'after the pattern of Jesus Christ' or 'in accordance with Jesus Christ,' not 'according to [the name of] Jesus Christ' as if invoking him. The standard is Christ's own love, not prayer in his name.
last_rejected.fix: that you love him in accordance with Jesus Christ
last_rejected.ruling: κατὰ Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν 'according to Jesus Christ' is standard; claim adds nuance but no meaning error

last_rejected.quote: that all of you be in likeness to him
last_rejected.source_quote: πάντας ὑμᾶς αὐτῷ ἐν ὁμοιότητι εἶναι
last_rejected.why: ἐν ὁμοιότητι εἶναι means 'be in likeness/subjection'—ὁμοιότης here carries the sense of conformity, submission, or being made like. 'In likeness to him' suggests resemblance; the force is 'be submissive to him' or 'be conformed to him' in the hierarchical relationship Ignatius stresses.
last_rejected.fix: that all of you be submissive to him
last_rejected.ruling: ἐν ὁμοιότητι 'in likeness to him' is literal and adequate; 'conformity/submission' is interpretation, not required

last_rejected.quote: Blessed is the one who granted you, being worthy, to have such a bishop
last_rejected.source_quote: εὐλογητὸς ὁ χαρισάμενος ὑμῖν ἀξίοις οὖσι τοιοῦτον ἐπίσκοπον κεκτῆσθαι
last_rejected.why: ἀξίοις οὖσι is concessive/causal: 'since you are worthy' or 'you being worthy.' The English 'being worthy' dangles ambiguously—does it modify 'the one who granted' or 'you'? The Greek clearly has God granting because/as they are worthy. 'Granted you, worthy as you are, to have' would clarify.
last_rejected.fix: Blessed is the one who granted you, since you are worthy, to have such a bishop
last_rejected.ruling: ἀξίοις οὖσι 'being worthy' is adequate; dangling is minor ambiguity, not a major error

polish.changed: Clarified the subject of the opening sentence, smoothed the transition between the first two sentences, and made the phrase 'kindred work' more natural as 'family work' while preserving the original sense.

notes.why: Reader may not realize 'council of elders' = 'elders' = presbyterion, and 'council of the apostles' is a typological parallel, not a different group.
notes.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note; clarify 'council of the apostles' as typology.

notes.why: 'Passible' (capable of suffering) vs 'passion' (suffering/death) are related but distinct; reader may miss Christological point.
notes.fix: Gloss 'passible' as 'capable of suffering' on first use.

notes.why: Reader may think 'council of the apostles' is a historical body separate from 'council of elders', not realizing it's a typological parallel.
notes.fix: Add note: 'council of the apostles' typologically parallels 'council of elders'.

notes.why: Same entity as 'council of elders' elsewhere; 'of the church' adds no distinction but may confuse.

notes.quote: the kindred work in the blood of God
notes.why: 'Kindred work' is an odd phrase; the Greek likely means 'family business' or 'kindred task,' but the sense is unclear.
notes.fix: Use 'family business' or 'kindred task' and add a note.

polish.changed: Clarified the opaque phrase about rekindling kinship by rendering it as 'the work that belongs to your kinship in the blood of God,' and smoothed sentence flow while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.why: Different animal metaphors for false teachers may blur into literal beasts of martyrdom.
notes.fix: Clarify metaphor vs. literal where possible.

notes.quote: you rekindled the kindred work in the blood of God
notes.why: 'Kindred work' is opaque; likely refers to kinship/love activated by Christ's blood.
notes.fix: Render as 'you rekindled your kinship in the blood of God.'

polish.changed: Repaired the broken syntax in the first paragraph by placing the completed action together, and clarified the flow of the opening greeting and prayer.

notes.quote: You are imitators of God, and you rekindled the work that belongs to your kinship, a work done in the blood of God, and completed it perfectly.
notes.why: Syntax broken: 'rekindled... and completed it' with intrusive appositive; 'blood of God' is striking but grammatically jarring.
notes.fix: Revise syntax: 'you rekindled and completed the work that belongs to your kinship, a work done in the blood of God.'

notes.quote: a work done in the blood of God
notes.why: 'Blood of God' is theologically striking but may be literal rendering of Greek; modern readers may think typo for 'blood of Christ' or 'Son of God'.
notes.fix: Retain with note, or consider 'blood of God's Son' if manuscript evidence allows.

polish.changed: Clarified 'just nature' as 'righteous character' and 'kinship' as 'spiritual family' to avoid misleading modern readings, while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.why: Same Greek word (presbyterion) rendered as 'council of elders' but also 'council of the bishop' and 'council of the apostles', which may confuse readers about whether these are the same body.
notes.fix: Use 'council of elders' consistently; note 'council of the apostles' is a different metaphor.

notes.why: In 2.6, elders stand 'in the place of the council of the apostles'—but 'council of the apostles' is not the same as 'council of elders', though both use 'council'. Reader may conflate them.
notes.fix: Clarify that 'council of the apostles' is a separate metaphor for the apostolic college.

notes.why: Unique phrase 'council of the bishop' in 5.8; elsewhere always 'council of elders'. Reader may wonder if this is a different body or a mistake.
notes.fix: Verify Greek; likely should be 'council of elders' or add note explaining this variant.

notes.quote: by a just nature according to faith and love
notes.why: 'Just nature' is odd; likely means 'righteous character' or 'just disposition'.

notes.quote: you rekindled the work that belongs to your kinship
facts: The Greek 'syngeneia' can mean kinship, but here likely refers to the familial bond among believers.
notes.why: 'Kinship' may suggest blood relation rather than the spiritual family of the church.

polish.changed: Clarified that Ignatius is the speaker throughout, smoothed the phrase 'rekindled the work' to 'revived the work,' and kept the striking phrase 'blood of God' as the source states it while preserving all claims and references exactly.

notes.why: Onesimus is identified as bishop only in sections 1.1 and 1.2; later just 'Onesimus' without title.
notes.fix: Consistently identify Onesimus as bishop on first mention in each letter context.

notes.why: Theologically striking but likely means 'blood of Christ/God's Son'; 'blood of God' is unusual and may startle reader.
notes.fix: Add note: 'early high Christology; or emend to "blood of Christ" if following some manuscripts.'

notes.quote: you rekindled the work that belongs to your spiritual family

variants.text: you rekindled the work that belongs to your spiritual family

notes.why: 'Rekindled the work' is an odd collocation; the Greek likely means 'revived' or 'restored.'
notes.fix: Consider 'you revived the work of your spiritual family.'

problems.fix: Reconsider the Greek; likely refers to 'kindled love' or 'family business.'

The syntax of the sentence has been revised to clarify that the work, not the kinship, is done in the blood of God.

problems.why: 'Mad dogs' and 'wild beasts' both describe false teachers, but 'beasts' also describes martyrdom animals; reader may conflate.

problems.why: 'Blood of God' is theologically striking but may seem blasphemous or misprinted; refers to Christ's blood.

fixed: The English 'rekindled by the blood of God' misreads the Greek: ἀναζωπυρήσαντες is active ('having rekindled'), and its object is τὸ συγγενικὸν ἔργον ('the kindred work'), not the Ephesians themselves. The phrase 'so natural to you' is also unclear. I restored the active construction and the object 'the work that belongs to your kinship,' matching the source. The 'blood of God' is retained as the source reads αἵματι θεοῦ.
The problems about 'mad dogs' and 'ten leopards' do not appear in this section; no edit needed.
The problem about 'blood of God' being theologically striking is a style concern, not a mistranslation; the source reads αἵματι θεοῦ, so I left it as 'blood of God.'
